lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide how semantic interfaces are discovered and permissioned for automation and AI callers (per-interface capability grants, manifest-declared exposure, user consent flows) before any semantic interface is shipped.
rationale: Shipping semantic interfaces without a permission design would grant automation clients de facto ambient authority.

text: AI must not operate by pretending to be a human moving a mouse; AI integration uses semantic interfaces and capabilities (see §42, §44).
Native UI platform must expose automation interfaces (§42, §45).
Allow applications to expose typed semantic interfaces defined in the native IDL (§14).
Implement a reference IDE/editor semantic interface with openProject(Project), searchSymbols(Query) -> Symbol[] and runTests(TestSelection) -> TestRun in the native editor (§60, §61).
Define a reference Mail semantic interface with search(Query) -> Message[], compose(Draft) and reply(Message, Draft).
Semantic interfaces must support automation clients.
Semantic interfaces must support cross-app integration.
Semantic interfaces must support AI clients (§44).
Semantic interfaces must never be implemented by synthesising mouse or keyboard input.
Implement a semantic interface discovery/registry service so one component can find another application's exposed interfaces.
Access to another application's semantic interface must require a capability granted by the user or policy.
AI must not be embedded as an omnipotent privileged process.
AI assistants operate through capabilities exactly like any other component.
Implement an assistant host component architecture where an agent runtime runs as an ordinary Component with an explicit capability set.
Define a Workspace.search(...) semantic interface returning Project capabilities.
Define a Project capability type transferable between Workspace, IDE and assistant components.
Support the action graph Workspace.search -> Project capability -> IDE.openProject -> IDE.runTests as an end-to-end demonstration.
AI actions must be typed (invoke IDL interfaces only).
AI actions must be composable into action graphs across applications.
Do not build AI integration before the semantic object model (§42) exists (§57).
Decide where assistant models execute (local via ComputeDevice/NPU, remote service) and confirm the OS provides only capability plumbing, not a model runtime (ADR).
Prototype the 'find the Postgres backup branch and run its tests' scenario end to end to validate the capability-based AI model.
Implement an automation layer built on semantic interfaces and typed capabilities.
Automation must not depend on GUI scraping or keyboard macros.
Define an application event model so apps can emit typed events such as Download.completed(file) and Meeting.start.
Implement a rule/trigger engine evaluating 'when event: if condition: action' rules.
Demonstrate the Download.completed -> if file.type == Archive -> Extractor.extract(file) automation.
Demonstrate the Meeting.start -> Notes.create(meeting) automation.
Automation rules must hold delegated typed capabilities (e.g. the file capability from the event) rather than ambient authority.
Decide the automation rule format: declarative rules, a scripting language, or Wasm automation modules (§13) (ADR).
Automation rule creation and changes must be recorded as system history events (§31).
Automations that run in the background require the explicit persistent-background capability (§21).
Do not build AI integration before the semantic object model exists; AI work is gated on SEM interface availability.
Semantic automation: user-defined rules over typed application interfaces (cross-ref §45).
Principle 12: semantic interfaces beat GUI automation.
Principle 13: AI receives capabilities, not omnipotence.
